verses.zh: （ 大 衛 與 兩 河 間 的 亞 蘭 並 瑣 巴 的 亞 蘭 爭 戰 的 時 候 ， 約 押 轉 回 ， 在 鹽 谷 攻 擊 以 東 ， 殺 了 一 萬 二 千 人 。 那 時 ， 大 衛 作 這 金 詩 叫 人 學 習 ， 交 與 伶 長 。 調 用 為 證 的 百 合 花 。 ） 神 啊 ， 你 丟 棄 了 我 們 ， 使 我 們 破 敗 ； 你 向 我 們 發 怒 ， 求 你 使 我 們 復 興 ！
verses.en: For the music director, according to the shushan-eduth style;[NOTE:1] a prayer[NOTE:2] of David written to instruct others.[NOTE:3] It was written when he fought against Aram Naharaim and Aram Zobah. That was when Joab turned back and struck down[NOTE:4] 12,000 Edomites[NOTE:5] in the Valley of Salt.[NOTE:6] O God, you have rejected us.[NOTE:7] You suddenly turned on us in your anger.[NOTE:8] Please restore us![NOTE:9]
notes: Psalm 60. The psalmist grieves over Israel’s humiliation, but in response to God’s assuring word, he asks for divine help in battle and expresses his confidence in victory.
The Hebrew expression means “lily of the testimony.” It may refer to a particular music style or to a tune title.
The precise meaning of the Hebrew word מִכְתָּם (miktam), which also appears in the heading to Pss 16, 56-59, is uncertain. HALOT 582-83 s.v. defines it as “inscription.”
Heb “to teach.”
In Josh 8:21 and Judg 20:48 the two verbs “turn back” and “strike down” are also juxtaposed. There they refer to a military counter-attack.
Heb “12,000 of Edom.” Perhaps one should read אֲרַם (’aram, “Aram”) here rather than אֱדוֹם (’edom, “Edom”).
The heading apparently refers to the military campaign recorded in 2 Sam 10 and 1 Chr 19.
You have rejected us. See Pss 43:2; 44:9, 23.
Heb “you broke out upon us, you were angry.”

verses.zh: 你 使 地 震 動 ， 而 且 崩 裂 ； 求 你 將 裂 口 醫 好 ， 因 為 地 搖 動 。
verses.en: You made the earth quake; you split it open.[NOTE:1] Repair its breaches, for it is ready to fall.[NOTE:2]
notes: The imperfect verbal form here expresses the psalmist’s wish or prayer.

The verb פָּצַם (patsam, “split open”) occurs only here in the OT. An Arabic cognate means “crack,” and an Aramaic cognate is used in Tg. Jer 22:14 with the meaning “break open, frame.” See BDB 822 s.v. and Jastrow 1205 s.v. פְּצַם.sn You made the earth quake; you split it open. The psalmist uses the imagery of an earthquake to describe the nation’s defeat.

verses.zh: 你 叫 你 的 民 遇 見 艱 難 ； 你 叫 我 們 喝 那 使 人 東 倒 西 歪 的 酒 。
verses.en: You have made your people experience hard times;[NOTE:1] you have made us drink intoxicating wine.[NOTE:2]
notes: It is ready to fall. The earth is compared to a wall that has been broken by the force of the earthquake (note the preceding line) and is ready to collapse.
Heb “you have caused your people to see [what is] hard.”

verses.zh: 你 把 旌 旗 賜 給 敬 畏 你 的 人 ， 可 以 為 真 理 揚 起 來 。 （ 細 拉 ）
verses.en: You have given your loyal followers[NOTE:1] a rallying flag,so that they might seek safety from the bow.[NOTE:2] (Selah)
notes: Heb “wine of staggering,” that is, intoxicating wine that makes one stagger in drunkenness. Intoxicating wine is here an image of divine judgment that makes its victims stagger like drunkards. See Isa 51:17-23.
Heb “those who fear you.”

verses.zh: 求 你 應 允 我 們 ， 用 右 手 拯 救 我 們 ， 好 叫 你 所 親 愛 的 人 得 救 。
verses.en: Deliver by your power[NOTE:1] and answer me,[NOTE:2] so that the ones you love may be safe.[NOTE:3]
notes: There is a ray of hope in that God has allowed his loyal followers to rally under a battle flag. The translation assumes the verb is from the root נוּס (nus, “flee”) used here in the Hitpolel in the sense of “find safety for oneself” (HALOT 681 s.v. נוס) or “take flight for oneself” (BDB 630-31 s.v. נוּס). Another option is to take the verb as a denominative from נֵס (nes, “flag”) and translate “that it may be displayed” (BDB 651 s.v. II נסס) or “that they may assemble under the banner” (HALOT 704 s.v. II נסס). Here קֹשֶׁט (qoshet) is taken as an Aramaized form of קֶשֶׁת (qeshet, “bow”; BDB 905-6 s.v. קֶשֶׁת), though some understand the homonymic קֹשְׁטְ (qoshet, “truth”) here (see Prov 22:21; cf. NASB). If one follows the latter interpretation, the line may be translated, “so that they might assemble under the banner for the sake of truth.”
Heb “right hand.”
The Qere (marginal reading) has “me,” while the Kethib (consonantal text) has “us.”

verses.zh: 神 已 經 指 著 他 的 聖 潔 說 （ 說 ： 或 譯 應 許 我 ） ： 我 要 歡 樂 ； 我 要 分 開 示 劍 ， 丈 量 疏 割 谷 。
verses.en: God has spoken in his sanctuary:[NOTE:1] “I will triumph. I will parcel out Shechem;the Valley of Sukkoth I will measure off.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “may be rescued.” The lines are actually reversed in the Hebrew text, “So that the ones you love may be rescued, deliver by your power and answer me.”
Heb “in his holy place.”

verses.zh: 基 列 是 我 的 ， 瑪 拿 西 也 是 我 的 。 以 法 蓮 是 護 衛 我 頭 的 ； 猶 大 是 我 的 杖 。
verses.en: Gilead belongs to me,as does Manasseh.[NOTE:1] Ephraim is my helmet,[NOTE:2] Judah my royal scepter.[NOTE:3]
notes: Shechem stands for the territory west of the Jordan, the Valley of Sukkoth for the region east of the Jordan.
Gilead was located east of the Jordan. Half of the tribe of Manasseh lived east of the Jordan in the region of Bashan.

Heb “the protection of my head.”sn Ephraim, named after one of Joseph’s sons, was one of two major tribes located west of the Jordan. By comparing Ephraim to a helmet, the Lord suggests that the Ephraimites played a primary role in the defense of his land.

verses.zh: 摩 押 是 我 的 沐 浴 盆 ； 我 要 向 以 東 拋 鞋 。 非 利 士 啊 ， 你 還 能 因 我 歡 呼 麼 ？
verses.en: Moab is my washbasin.[NOTE:1] I will make Edom serve me.[NOTE:2] I will shout in triumph over Philistia.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Judah, like Ephraim, was the other major tribe west of the Jordan. The Davidic king, symbolized here by the royal scepter, came from this tribe.
The metaphor of the washbasin, used to rinse one’s hands and feet, suggests that Moab, in contrast to Israel’s elevated position (vv. 6-7), would be reduced to the status of a servant.

Heb “over Edom I will throw my sandal.” The point of the metaphor is not entirely clear. Some interpret this as idiomatic for “taking possession of,” i.e., “I will take possession of Edom.” Others translate עַל (ʿal) as “to” and understand this as referring to a master throwing his dirty sandal to a servant so that the latter might dust it off.

verses.zh: 誰 能 領 我 進 堅 固 城 ？ 誰 能 引 我 到 以 東 地 ？
verses.en: Who will lead me into the fortified city?Who will bring me to Edom?[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “over me, O Philistia, shout in triumph.” The translation follows the text of Ps 108:9. When the initial עֲלֵיוֹ (ʿaleyo, “over”) was misread as עָלַי (ʿalay, “over me”), the first person verb form was probably altered to an imperative to provide better sense to the line.

verses.zh: 神 啊 ， 你 不 是 丟 棄 了 我 們 麼 ？ 神 啊 ， 你 不 和 我 們 的 軍 兵 同 去 麼 ？
verses.en: Have you not rejected us, O God?O God, you do not go into battle with our armies.

verses.zh: 求 你 幫 助 我 們 攻 擊 敵 人 ， 因 為 人 的 幫 助 是 枉 然 的 。
verses.en: Give us help against the enemy,for any help men might offer is futile.[NOTE:1]
notes: In v. 9 the psalmist speaks again and acknowledges his need for help in battle. He hopes God will volunteer, based on the affirmation of sovereignty over Edom in v. 8, but he is also aware that God has seemingly rejected the nation (v. 10, see also v. 1).

verses.zh: 我 們 倚 靠 神 才 得 施 展 大 能 ， 因 為 踐 踏 我 們 敵 人 的 就 是 他 。
verses.en: By God’s power we will conquer;[NOTE:1] he will trample down[NOTE:2] our enemies.
notes: Heb “and futile [is] the deliverance of man.”
Heb “in God we will accomplish strength.” The statement refers here to military success (see Num 24:18; 1 Sam 14:48; Pss 108:13; 118:15-16).
